messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Defining covariance matrix in the model block vs. the transformed parameters block
parts:
The transformed parameters block

1) saves the variables you define in its top level,
2) also checks constraints.

If you don't need either, you can put your code in the model block.

Best,

Tamas

On Sat, May 21 2016, mjflores wrote:

> Hi everyone,
> I am working on coding up a spatial model, and I would like to define the
> prior such that the variance-covariance matrix Sigma is constructed using
> an exponential covariance function, i.e. [Sigma]_ij = exp(-rho * ||d_i -
> d_j||), where ||d_i - d_j|| is just the distance between two spatial points.
>
> Since I'm basically fitting a gaussian process, I know that I probably want
> to define the covariance matrix in the model block, but I just had a
> conceptual question about defining these things in the transformed
> parameters block versus the model block. From the 8schools example, we can
> see that the theta parameters are defined in the transformed parameters
> block
>
> parameters {
> real mu;
> real<lower=0> tau;
> real eta[J];
> }
> transformed parameters {
> real theta[J];
> for (j in 1:J)
> theta[j] <- mu + tau * eta[j];
> }
> model {
> eta ~ normal(0, 1);
> y ~ normal(theta, sigma);
> }
>
> However, just for a couple examples from the documentation, on page 78 with
> the AR(k) model the mean parameters mu are defined in the model block. This
> is also the case for the covariance matrix in section 14.3 on fitting
> gaussian models. I'm just wondering if there is a difference between
> defining these things in the transformed parameters block versus the model
> block aside from saving all the transformed parameters in the output. So
> basically in the above model, if you put the theta parameters into the
> model block, would the model still be the same?
